modules.title: 11.1 Foundations: Homologous Series, Nomenclature and Isomerism
modules.html:
Organic chemistry is the chemistry of carbon compounds, excluding the oxides of carbon, trioxocarbonates, hydrogentrioxocarbonates, cyanides and carbides. Carbon's ability to catenate (bond to itself indefinitely) plus its tetravalency give rise to millions of compounds.

Key definitions

  • Homologous series: a family of compounds with the same general formula, similar chemical properties, and successive members differing by \(CH_2\) (relative molecular mass 14), with a gradual change in physical properties.
  • Functional group: the atom or group of atoms that determines the chemical properties of the series.
  • Saturated compound: contains only single carbon-carbon bonds; unsaturated contains a double or triple bond.
  • Isomerism: compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural formulae — chain, position and functional-group isomerism.

The main homologous series

SeriesGeneral formulaFunctional groupSuffix
Alkanes\(C_nH_{2n+2}\)C–C only-ane
Alkenes\(C_nH_{2n}\)C=C-ene
Alkynes\(C_nH_{2n-2}\)C≡C-yne
Alkanols\(C_nH_{2n+1}OH\)–OH-anol
Alkanals\(C_nH_{2n}O\)–CHO-anal
Alkanones\(C_nH_{2n}O\)>C=O-anone
Alkanoic acids\(C_nH_{2n+1}COOH\)–COOH-anoic acid
Alkanoates (esters)\(RCOOR'\)–COO–-yl -anoate

IUPAC nomenclature in four steps

  1. Find the longest continuous carbon chain containing the functional group; that gives the stem (meth-, eth-, prop-, but-, pent-, hex-, hept-, oct-, non-, dec-).
  2. Number the chain from the end that gives the functional group (or, failing that, the first substituent) the lowest number.
  3. Name and number the substituents alphabetically, using di-, tri-, tetra- for repeats.
  4. Combine: substituents + stem + suffix, e.g. \(CH_3CH(CH_3)CH_2CH_3\) is 2-methylbutane, and \(CH_3CH(OH)CH_2CH_3\) is butan-2-ol.

Isomerism worked out

\(C_4H_{10}\) has two isomers: butane (\(CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_3\)) and 2-methylpropane. \(C_5H_{12}\) has three. \(C_4H_8\) as an alkene gives but-1-ene, but-2-ene and 2-methylpropene (chain and position isomerism), plus cyclobutane as a functional isomer. \(C_2H_6O\) illustrates functional-group isomerism: ethanol (\(CH_3CH_2OH\), boiling point \(78^{\circ}C\)) and methoxymethane (\(CH_3OCH_3\), boiling point \(-24^{\circ}C\)); the huge difference is due to hydrogen bonding in the alcohol.

Sources of organic compounds

Petroleum (crude oil) is separated by fractional distillation into refinery gas, petrol, kerosene, diesel, lubricating oil and bitumen, in order of increasing boiling point and chain length. Cracking breaks long-chain alkanes into short-chain alkanes and alkenes for petrol and plastics; reforming converts straight chains into branched or cyclic ones to raise the octane number.
examples: Draw and name the three isomers of C5H12.

modules.title: 11.2 Hydrocarbons: Alkanes, Alkenes and Alkynes
modules.html:
Alkanes — the paraffins, \(C_nH_{2n+2}\)

Alkanes are saturated, tetrahedral (\(109.5^{\circ}\)), non-polar and relatively unreactive ("paraffin" = little affinity). Physical trend: \(C_1\)–\(C_4\) gases, \(C_5\)–\(C_{17}\) liquids, above that solids; boiling point rises with chain length because van der Waals forces increase, and branching lowers boiling point by reducing contact area.

  • Combustion: complete, \(CH_4 + 2O_2 \rightarrow CO_2 + 2H_2O\); incomplete gives \(CO\) or soot.
  • Substitution with halogens in ultraviolet light (free-radical mechanism): \(CH_4 + Cl_2 \xrightarrow{uv} CH_3Cl + HCl\), continuing to \(CCl_4\).
  • Cracking: \(C_{10}H_{22} \rightarrow C_8H_{18} + C_2H_4\).
  • They do not react with acids, alkalis, \(KMnO_4\) or bromine water in the dark — the classic contrast with alkenes.
  • Laboratory preparation of methane: soda lime plus sodium ethanoate, \(CH_3COONa + NaOH \rightarrow CH_4 + Na_2CO_3\).

Alkenes — the olefins, \(C_nH_{2n}\)

The \(C=C\) group is planar with \(120^{\circ}\) bond angles and contains a weak pi bond that is the site of attack. Preparation: dehydration of ethanol with concentrated \(H_2SO_4\) at \(170^{\circ}C\), or cracking of alkanes.

  • Addition of hydrogen (Ni, \(180^{\circ}C\)): \(C_2H_4 + H_2 \rightarrow C_2H_6\) — the basis of margarine manufacture.
  • Addition of bromine: red-brown bromine water is decolourised — the standard test for unsaturation.
  • Addition of water (steam, \(H_3PO_4\), 300°C, 60 atm) gives ethanol industrially.
  • Oxidation by cold dilute \(KMnO_4\) gives a diol and decolourises the purple solution (Baeyer's test).
  • Polymerisation: \(n(CH_2{=}CH_2) \rightarrow (-CH_2-CH_2-)_n\), polyethene; similarly propene gives polypropene and chloroethene gives PVC.

Alkynes, \(C_nH_{2n-2}\)

Ethyne is prepared from calcium dicarbide and water: \(CaC_2 + 2H_2O \rightarrow C_2H_2 + Ca(OH)_2\). It is linear (\(180^{\circ}\)), burns with a very hot sooty flame (oxy-acetylene welding at about \(3000^{\circ}C\)), undergoes addition like alkenes but requires two moles of reagent, and its terminal hydrogen is weakly acidic, giving a red precipitate with ammoniacal copper(I) chloride.

Distinguishing the three

TestAlkaneAlkeneAlkyne
Bromine waterNo change (dark)DecolourisedDecolourised
Cold dilute \(KMnO_4\)No changeDecolourisedDecolourised
Ammoniacal \(CuCl\)No changeNo changeRed precipitate
FlameFairly cleanLuminous, some sootVery sooty
examples: Describe a chemical test to distinguish ethane from ethene.
Write the equation for the polymerisation of chloroethene.

modules.title: 11.3 Alkanols, Alkanoic Acids, Esters, Soaps and Polymers
modules.html:
Alkanols (alcohols), \(R{-}OH\)

Classified as primary (\(RCH_2OH\)), secondary (\(R_2CHOH\)) and tertiary (\(R_3COH\)). Hydrogen bonding gives them much higher boiling points and far greater water solubility than alkanes of similar mass.

  • Preparation: fermentation of glucose with zymase from yeast, \(C_6H_{12}O_6 \rightarrow 2C_2H_5OH + 2CO_2\) (25–37°C, anaerobic), or hydration of ethene industrially.
  • With sodium: \(2C_2H_5OH + 2Na \rightarrow 2C_2H_5ONa + H_2\) — effervescence but no reaction with \(NaOH\), showing alcohols are neutral, not acidic.
  • Oxidation with acidified \(K_2Cr_2O_7\): primary → alkanal → alkanoic acid (orange turns green); secondary → alkanone; tertiary → no oxidation. This is the standard way to classify an unknown alcohol.
  • Dehydration: concentrated \(H_2SO_4\) at 170°C gives the alkene; at 140°C it gives the ether.
  • Esterification: alcohol + acid, acid catalyst, gives a sweet-smelling ester and water.
  • Iodoform (triiodomethane) test: ethanol and other \(CH_3CH(OH)-\) compounds give a yellow precipitate with iodine and \(NaOH\).

Alkanoic acids, \(R{-}COOH\)

These are weak acids that nevertheless show all the typical acid reactions: they turn litmus red, liberate \(CO_2\) from trioxocarbonates (a test that distinguishes them from alcohols and phenols), give hydrogen with reactive metals and form salts with alkalis. Examples: methanoic acid (ant stings), ethanoic acid (vinegar), and the long-chain fatty acids palmitic, stearic and oleic acid found in oils and fats.

Esters (alkyl alkanoates)

Esterification is reversible and acid-catalysed:

\(CH_3COOH + C_2H_5OH \underset{}{\overset{conc. H_2SO_4}{\rightleftharpoons}} CH_3COOC_2H_5 + H_2O\) — ethyl ethanoate, smelling of nail-polish remover.

Esters are neutral, sweet-smelling liquids used as flavourings, perfumes and solvents. Hydrolysis with dilute acid reverses the reaction; with alkali it goes to completion and is called saponification.

Soaps and detergents

Soap is made by boiling animal fat or vegetable oil (an ester of propane-1,2,3-triol) with concentrated \(NaOH\):

fat + \(3NaOH \rightarrow\) 3 sodium alkanoate (soap) + glycerol.

Common salt is then added to salt out the soap. A soap molecule has a long hydrophobic hydrocarbon tail and an ionic hydrophilic head; the tail dissolves in grease while the head stays in water, so the grease is lifted off and held in an emulsion. Soap fails in hard water because \(Ca^{2+}\) and \(Mg^{2+}\) precipitate insoluble scum. Detergents (alkylbenzenesulphonates) work in hard water because their calcium salts are soluble, but branched-chain detergents are non-biodegradable and cause foaming in rivers, while their phosphate builders cause eutrophication.

Macromolecules

Addition polymers: polyethene, polypropene, PVC, polystyrene, PTFE — from unsaturated monomers, no by-product. Condensation polymers: nylon, terylene, proteins, starch and cellulose — a small molecule such as water is eliminated at each link.
examples: Explain how you would classify an unknown alcohol as primary, secondary or tertiary.
Describe the manufacture of soap from palm oil and state the role of common salt.

modules.title: 11.4 Calculations, Reaction Maps and Practical Observations
modules.html:
Organic questions in WAEC/NECO reward accurate structures, correct reagents and clean calculations. Use the routines below.

Determining a formula from combustion data

Example: An organic compound contains 40% C, 6.7% H and 53.3% O by mass, and its relative molecular mass is 60. Find its molecular formula. (\(C=12, H=1, O=16\)).

CHO
Mass %406.753.3
÷ atomic mass3.336.73.33
÷ smallest121

Empirical formula \(CH_2O\) (mass 30). \(60/30 = 2\), so the molecular formula is \(\mathbf{C_2H_4O_2}\) — ethanoic acid.

Volume of oxygen for combustion

Example: What volume of oxygen at s.t.p. is needed to burn \(5\ dm^3\) of ethane completely?

\(2C_2H_6 + 7O_2 \rightarrow 4CO_2 + 6H_2O\). By Gay-Lussac's law, volumes are in the mole ratio: \(V(O_2) = 5 \times 7/2 = \mathbf{17.5\ dm^3}\), and \(V(CO_2) = 5\times2 = 10\ dm^3\).

Reaction map to memorise

alkane --(uv, Cl2)--> halogenoalkane --(aq NaOH)--> alkanol
alkene --(H2/Ni)--> alkane        alkene --(H2O, H3PO4)--> alkanol
alkanol --(K2Cr2O7/H+)--> alkanal --(further ox.)--> alkanoic acid
alkanoic acid + alkanol --(conc H2SO4)--> ester + water
ester + NaOH --> soap + alkanol/glycerol (saponification)
alkanol --(conc H2SO4, 170 C)--> alkene --(polymerisation)--> plastic

Key laboratory observations

  • Bromine water decolourised → unsaturation (alkene or alkyne).
  • Effervescence with \(Na_2CO_3\) → carboxylic acid (alcohols give none).
  • Effervescence with sodium metal only → alcohol.
  • Orange dichromate turning green on warming → primary or secondary alcohol.
  • Sweet fruity smell after warming acid + alcohol + \(H_2SO_4\) → ester formed.
  • Yellow precipitate with \(I_2/NaOH\) → ethanol, or a methyl ketone.

Uses and everyday relevance in Nigeria

Ethanol from cassava and sugar-cane fermentation is blended with petrol as a biofuel; palm oil and shea butter are the local raw materials for soap-making; polyethene "pure water" sachets and PVC pipes are addition polymers whose non-biodegradability creates the plastic-waste problem now tackled by recycling and bans on single-use bags. Natural gas from the Niger Delta is largely methane, used for cooking (LPG) and in fertiliser and methanol plants at Eleme and Escravos.

Marking-scheme discipline

  1. Draw displayed structures when asked for structural formulae — show every bond.
  2. State reagent and condition (catalyst, temperature) — each is a separate mark.
  3. Balance organic equations by carbon, then hydrogen, then oxygen last.
  4. Do not write "alcohol" when the question asks for a name: write "ethanol".
examples: Determine the molecular formula of a compound with 52.2% C, 13.0% H, 34.8% O and M = 46.
Give the reagents and conditions for converting ethene to ethyl ethanoate in three steps.

quiz.q: Organic chemistry is the study of
options: carbon compounds except oxides, trioxocarbonates and carbides
quiz.solution: The simple carbon compounds are treated as inorganic.

quiz.q: The ability of carbon atoms to bond to one another indefinitely is called
quiz.solution: Catenation gives rise to the vast number of organic compounds.

quiz.q: Successive members of a homologous series differ by
quiz.solution: The difference is CH2, or 14 mass units.

quiz.q: The general formula of alkanes is
quiz.solution: Saturated hydrocarbons have 2n+2 hydrogen atoms.

quiz.q: The general formula of alkenes is
quiz.solution: One double bond removes two hydrogen atoms.

quiz.q: The functional group of alkanoic acids is
quiz.solution: The carboxyl group defines the acid series.

quiz.q: The IUPAC name of CH3CH(CH3)CH2CH3 is
quiz.solution: The longest chain has four carbons with a methyl on carbon 2.

quiz.q: The number of structural isomers of C4H10 is
quiz.solution: Butane and 2-methylpropane.

quiz.q: Ethanol and methoxymethane are examples of
quiz.solution: Same molecular formula C2H6O but different functional groups.

quiz.q: Ethanol boils much higher than methoxymethane because of
quiz.solution: The O-H group allows intermolecular hydrogen bonds.

quiz.q: Crude oil is separated into fractions by
quiz.solution: The fractions differ in boiling range.

quiz.q: Cracking of alkanes produces
quiz.solution: Long chains break to give useful short chains and alkenes.

quiz.q: Alkanes are described as paraffins because they are
quiz.solution: Paraffin means little affinity.

quiz.q: The reaction of methane with chlorine in ultraviolet light is
quiz.solution: A hydrogen atom is replaced by chlorine in a free-radical chain.

quiz.q: Methane is prepared in the laboratory by heating sodium ethanoate with
quiz.solution: Decarboxylation with soda lime gives methane.

quiz.q: The bond angle in ethene is about
quiz.solution: The trigonal planar sp2 carbon gives 120 degrees.

quiz.q: The test for unsaturation is decolourisation of
quiz.solution: Bromine adds across the double bond, losing its colour.

quiz.q: Ethene reacts with hydrogen over nickel to give
quiz.solution: Catalytic hydrogenation gives the saturated alkane.

quiz.q: Hardening of vegetable oil into margarine involves
quiz.solution: Hydrogen adds to the C=C bonds of the unsaturated oil.

quiz.q: Polymerisation of ethene gives
quiz.solution: Ethene is the monomer of polyethene.

quiz.q: Ethyne is prepared from
quiz.solution: CaC2 + 2H2O gives C2H2 and Ca(OH)2.

quiz.q: The bond angle in ethyne is
quiz.solution: The triple bond makes the molecule linear.

quiz.q: The oxy-acetylene flame is used for welding because it
quiz.solution: It reaches about 3000 degrees Celsius.

quiz.q: Ethyne gives a red precipitate with
quiz.solution: Terminal alkynes have a weakly acidic hydrogen.

quiz.q: A secondary alkanol on oxidation gives
quiz.solution: Only primary alcohols oxidise all the way to acids.

quiz.q: Tertiary alkanols
quiz.solution: There is no hydrogen on the carbon bearing the OH group.

quiz.q: The conversion of glucose to ethanol by yeast is
quiz.solution: The enzyme zymase catalyses anaerobic fermentation.

quiz.q: Ethanol reacts with sodium to give
quiz.solution: Sodium ethanoxide and hydrogen are formed.

quiz.q: Dehydration of ethanol with concentrated H2SO4 at 170 C gives
quiz.solution: Elimination of water gives the alkene.

quiz.q: Which reagent distinguishes ethanoic acid from ethanol?
quiz.solution: Only the acid gives carbon dioxide with a carbonate.

quiz.q: The reaction of an alkanol with an alkanoic acid is called
quiz.solution: An ester and water are formed reversibly.

quiz.q: The catalyst used in esterification is
quiz.solution: Concentrated acid catalyses and removes water.

quiz.q: Esters are noted for their
quiz.solution: They are used as flavourings and perfumes.

quiz.q: The alkaline hydrolysis of an ester is called
quiz.solution: It produces soap when the ester is a fat.

quiz.q: Soap is the sodium or potassium salt of
quiz.solution: Fatty acid salts are soaps.

quiz.q: The by-product of soap manufacture from fat is
quiz.solution: Propane-1,2,3-triol, glycerol, is released.

quiz.q: Common salt is added during soap making to
quiz.solution: Soap is less soluble in concentrated brine and separates.

quiz.q: The hydrocarbon end of a soap molecule is
quiz.solution: It dissolves in grease, while the ionic head stays in water.

quiz.q: Soap forms scum in hard water because of
quiz.solution: Insoluble calcium and magnesium salts of the fatty acid precipitate.

quiz.q: Detergents lather in hard water because their calcium salts are
quiz.solution: No scum forms with alkylbenzenesulphonates.

quiz.q: A disadvantage of some detergents is that they
quiz.solution: Branched chains resist bacterial breakdown.

quiz.q: Which is a condensation polymer?
quiz.solution: Nylon eliminates a small molecule at each linkage.

quiz.q: Which is an addition polymer?
quiz.solution: Propene monomers add without losing atoms.

quiz.q: A compound with 40% C, 6.7% H and 53.3% O and M = 60 has the molecular formula
quiz.solution: Empirical CH2O has mass 30; 60/30 = 2.

quiz.q: What volume of oxygen at s.t.p. burns 5 dm3 of ethane completely?
How many carbon dioxide molecules are formed per molecule of propane burnt?
quiz.solution: C3H8 + 5O2 gives 3CO2 + 4H2O.

quiz.q: Which alcohol gives a yellow precipitate with iodine and sodium hydroxide?
quiz.solution: The iodoform test is positive for CH3CH(OH) groups.

quiz.q: Vinegar contains
quiz.solution: Vinegar is a dilute solution of ethanoic acid.

quiz.q: The main component of natural gas is
quiz.solution: Methane makes up most of natural gas.

quiz.q: PVC is made from the monomer
quiz.solution: Chloroethene, vinyl chloride, polymerises to PVC.
